title: Twenty-two Seasons and One Empty Bed
subtitle: 健康与医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）
meta: 主题语境：健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）　|　核心词汇：disease　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 disease 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1944 the physician ① named a disease that no hospital in the county would have admitted, and he said the naming was the whole of the ward. The ② disease, meaning the illness and not the outbreak, ran twenty-two seasons and stayed unentered in the register; a disease, he said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ disease in that ward had the same empty bed beside it, and the ④ disease at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter admissions and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever recorded twice. A disease, the nurse said, is nine parts watching and one part somebody willing to name; the physician said the watching is the part that fills twenty-two seasons.

The inspector meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the disease was the whole of the report, meaning the outbreak and not the illness. The ⑥ disease, meaning the outbreak and not any of that, is the only thing in a report that everybody counts and nobody cures; disease, she said, is either something you name or the only word that means both an illness and an outbreak. She said the outbreak is the part they remember.

By 1952 the ⑦ disease had become a line in a table, and the table had become an argument about the empty bed. The ⑧ disease of the whole thing, the physician wrote in December, was one ward and twenty-two seasons of watching; disease, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to watch. She said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ disease I remember is the one at the end, which was cured in 1966 and is still described as the strangest in the ward. A ⑩ disease, the nurse said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being understood; every disease, she said, is an outbreak that has agreed to look like an illness. She said the outbreak was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 疾病；病（指病房里诊断的那一种）
B. n. 疾病（指那种病症本身，与那场疫情相对）
C. 固定搭配：name a disease 说出（诊断）一种疾病
D. n. 疾病（指留给冬季入院病人的那一种）
E. n. 疾病；病患（抽象总称，指一间病房的全部病症）
F. n. 疾病（指统计表上写到、被列名的那一种）
G. n. （疾病的）暴发；流行（指报告里被统计的那场）
H. n. 疫情（抽象总称，指人人统计却无人治愈的那场）

items.q: named a disease that no hospital in the county would have admitted
The disease, meaning the illness and not the outbreak
the disease was the whole of the report
the disease had become a line in a table
The disease of the whole thing
A disease, the nurse said in 1968

answers.why: name a disease 意为“说出（诊断）一种疾病”，1944 年医生诊断了一种全郡没有一家医院肯承认的疾病。
disease 意为“疾病”，指那种病症本身而不是那场疫情，它在病房里历经二十二个季节而未登记。
disease 意为“疾病”，指那间病房里每一种疾病，每一种旁边都有同一张空床。
disease 意为“疾病”，指留给冬季入院病人的那一种，是唯一有人记录过两次的。
disease 意为“暴发、流行”，指报告里被统计的那场，视察员说这场疫情就是那份报告的全部。
disease 意为“疫情”，指人人统计却无人治愈的那场而不是那种病症本身，是报告里人人都统计、却无人治愈的东西。
disease 意为“疾病”，指统计表上写到、被列名的那一种，到 1952 年这种疾病成了统计表里的一行。
disease 意为“疾病、病患”，医生十二月写道，整件事的病患是一间病房和二十二个季节的观察。
disease 意为“疾病”，我记得的是末尾那一种，1966 年治愈，至今仍被说成病房里最奇的一种。
disease 为抽象总称，护士 1968 年说，一种疾病是唯一会因为被理解而变得更好的东西。
